Capital exposure before you hold keys

Two different kinds of easy. Floareá asks the least before keys — 30%, of which 20% is the booking and only 10% falls due across two instalments in 2026–27. It also carries the largest payment at the end: 70% on completion, typically the point a mortgage is drawn. Celesto's 1% a month is the opposite trade — more capital in overall, but funded from monthly income rather than a lump sum.

Floareá Skies · Mashriq Elite

The developer

Mashriq Elite
Developments

20+ yrsGroup history
4thVenture

The property arm of Al Mashriq Group — a diversified house with over two decades across real estate, project development and telecommunications, and a network spanning the UAE, United States, Europe, Singapore and Saudi Arabia. Design, architecture and delivery sit under one roof in their own design centre.

Floareá Skies is their fourth venture, positioned as the project that sets their benchmark. The record is short but real: a project launched September 2023 was handed over in August 2025, with further launches in June 2024 and February 2025, and announced chapters in Dubai Islands and Dubailand.

Citrus courtyards, one kilometre of green

Marwan Wareth

Arancia · BEYOND · OMNIYAT

The developer

BEYOND

The premium residential brand of OMNIYAT Group, founded in Dubai in 2005 — the group behind the city's ultra-prime waterfront portfolio.

AED 4bnMasterplan value
70%Open landscape

The Yards is BEYOND's master-planned destination in City of Arabia: 2.3 million sqft of gross floor area, 1,560 residences, organised along a one-kilometre green spine, with 70% of the total area given to open landscape. Mediterranean-inspired, with its own school, clinic, mosque, farm, gardens and retail — a complete community rather than an apartment block with a pool.

Arancia is the first cluster to launch inside it: 272 residences across three low-rise buildings, G+6 and G+7, arranged around a central green valley.

Celesto Tower 4 · Al Tarrad

The developer

Al Tarrad
Development

4thIn the series
99.99%Of allowed GFA used

Al Tarrad runs a focused, repeatable formula: mid-rise residential towers in Dubailand aimed at the investor and entry end-user market — fully furnished, smart-home fitted, priced below the city's mid-market. Celesto 4 is the fourth in a numbered series, which tells you the model works well enough to keep running.

The submitted design package is itself a confidence signal: a full climate and solar study, site accessibility and land-use analysis, verified area calculations against permitted GFA, a reconciled unit matrix and complete floor plans. Residential GFA comes in at 22,309.05 sqm against an allowed 22,311.00.

What each one costs you

No project here is perfect

Every option has a real weakness. These are the ones worth knowing before signing, not after.

Floareá Skies

The catch
  • Boutique developer with a thin delivery record — the real risk on this deal
  • JVC is Dubai's most crowded pipeline: 16,800–22,000 units to 2028, so rents may soften 5–10% right at handover
  • 70% falls due on completion — the largest single payment of the three, usually the point a mortgage is drawn
  • AED 1.2M all-in for the mid yield of the three at 5.7% — a size-and-timing buy more than an income buy
  • Service charge of AED 14/sqft is above Celesto's 12 — the rooftop pool and meditation deck cost something to run

Arancia

The catch
  • At the confirmed AED 1.45M price it is the dearest per foot (1,933) and the lowest yield of the three at 5.2%
  • Q1 2029 handover — the longest wait. Four years before a dirham of rent
  • 1,560 units across the masterplan: your client's resale competes with the developer's own later phases at newer stock
  • Inland City of Arabia — resale depends on the community delivering as drawn
  • Not furnished, unlike the other two
  • The only one with no published service charge, and the heaviest amenity and landscape load of the three

Celesto Tower 4

The catch
  • 414 units in one building — more than double Floareá. At handover the 1BR competes with 179 identical neighbours
  • 39% of the building is studios — investor-heavy, higher churn, weaker owner-occupier base at resale
  • The 1BR is the smallest of the three at 590 sqft
  • One parking space per apartment, no resident surplus
  • Least established developer, delivery record on Celesto 1–3 unverified

Marwan Wareth

The decision

Three different propositions, not a ranking

The numbers land close enough that they don't decide this. What decides it is which of these three sentences sounds most like you.

“I want the biggest apartment, the earliest keys, and the least money tied up until then.”
Floareá Skies
Q1 2028, 837 sqft, only 30% before handover — and the developer will talk about the price.
“I want the best address and the strongest rent, and I can wait until 2029.”
Arancia
AED 90,000 a year — the highest rent of the three — OMNIYAT's brand and the only true community. Priced for it at 1,933/sqft.
“I want the smallest cheque, paid monthly, and the best yield.”
Celesto Tower 4
6.8% on the least capital, 1% a month for 30 months, and metro at one minute.
My read, on the confirmed prices: yield-first, it is Celesto 4 at 6.8% on the smallest cheque. Floareá sits in the middle at 5.7% with the earliest keys and the biggest apartment. Arancia at AED 1.45M is the premium play — the strongest rent and name at 5.2%, bought for the address, not the yield. Still open: Celesto's price is an estimate; Arancia's service charge is unpublished.
